$comment: capture-plan.json: which devices capture which screens in which locales, and how each screen is reached (CONTRACT.md 10.2). Paths are relative to the plan's own folder. Settings (locales, appearance, clock, statusBar, seed, flatten) resolve plan, then the device, then the screen, then the screen's overrides for that device's id or platform (each later one wins). staging (agreed with the user first) and each screen's state and verify say how the app is set up and what each screen must show. Uses only the subset appstores_lib/schema.py validates.

out.$comment: The captures' folder: <out>/<locale>/<device id>/<screen id>.png and <out>/capture-report.json. Default 'captures'.

clock.$comment: The status bar's time: 'H:MM' or 'HH:MM' (24-hour), or an ISO date-time. Default '09:41'.

statusBar.$comment: clean: the plan's clock, full battery and signal, no notifications (simctl status_bar, Android's demo mode). as-is: left alone. Default clean.

seed.$comment: Passed to the app as ScreenshotSeed (a launch argument, an intent extra, a query parameter).

flatten.$comment: The colour a picture with an alpha channel is flattened onto (#RRGGBB). Default #000000, as a device's masked corners are.

app.$comment: The app on each platform. A device uses the entry for its platform, else its family's (ipados/tvos/watchos/visionos -> ios), merged with the device's own 'app'.
A built .app to install (simulators) or open (macOS).

processName.$comment: macOS: the process name System Events knows it by (default: the .app's name).

activity.$comment: The activity launch starts ('.MainActivity' or a full class name).

apk.$comment: An APK to install before the screens (adb install -r).

url.$comment: The app's address (on this machine: drivers reach nothing else). launch opens it; url steps resolve against it.

kind.$comment: phone, tablet, desktop, tv, watch or xr: which store slot its pictures are for (check_captures.py --rules).

width.$comment: The exact pixel size this device promises (from the store's rules). Any other size is failed, never resized.

target.$comment: The driver's own settings (simctl: deviceType, runtime, udid, display, localeScope; adb: systemImage, profile, avd, serial, wmSize, density, deviceLocale, navigation, statusBarMobile, statusBarCheck, adb, emulator, avdmanager; agents: agentPort, agentPlatform, appName, agentTimeout, host, screenshot; appium: server, capabilities; chrome: scale, viewport, mobile; macos: scale). references/config.md lists them all.

app.$comment: Merged over the plan's app entry for this device's platform.

state.$comment: What the screen must show, in plain words (whose data, which state): agreed with the user; in staging.md and the report.

staging.$comment: false: this screen gets neither the staging's seed nor its launch values (an onboarding screen, say).

devices.$comment: Only these devices (ids). Default: every device.

locales.$comment: Only these of the device's locales.

overrides.$comment: Per device id or platform: settings or steps that differ there ({"android": {"steps": [...]}}). A device id's entry wins over its platform's.

element.$comment: One of id (accessibility identifier / automation id / resource id / test id), text, label, xpath or css (web).

timeout.$comment: Seconds to wait for it. Default 10.

appPath.$comment: A path inside the app's own data: iOS relative to its data container (Library/Caches/app.db), Android to /data/data/<package> (files/app.db, cache/app.db); one, or one per platform.

verify.$comment: An element (or a list) that must be on screen before the shot; otherwise the shot is missed, 'wrong state'. A driver that can't see elements reports it unchecked.

staging.$comment: How the app is staged for the captures, agreed with the user before the plan is run (references/staging.md). capture.py puts launch and seed into every screen, grants the permissions, checks the account's variables are set, and captures more than one screen only once confirmed is set; capture.py --write-staging writes it readable as staging.md.

doc.$comment: The readable copy beside the plan (default staging.md).

confirmed.$comment: Set when the user has seen one screen captured with this staging and agreed it. Until then a run captures one screen only.

account.$comment: How the app is signed in: none, guest (guest mode), bypass (a debug sign-in bypass) or demo (a demo account, its sign-in only by the names of environment variables; never a real person's account).

env.$comment: Variables holding the demo account's sign-in (DEMO_USER, DEMO_PASSWORD): checked before a run, usable in launch values as ${NAME}, masked in logs and reports.

seed.$comment: Where the demo data comes from: command (run before each screen, like a script step), file (copied into the app's own data before each screen, an appFile step), launch (the app seeds itself from a launch argument: put it in launch.args), backend (a staging server with invented data) or none.

when.$comment: each-screen (default) or once (before each device's first screen).

launch.$comment: Added to every launch step (a step's own args and env win): the screenshot mode's switch, a sign-in bypass, a fake server's address. ${NAME} takes one of account.env's variables.

skip.$comment: What's skipped and how: onboarding, paywalls, rating prompts, what's-new sheets, tooltips.

permissions.$comment: Granted before launch, revoked after, by platform: simctl privacy services on Apple (photos, location, contacts, ...), Android permission names (android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS).

flags.$comment: Feature flags the screens need, and how they're set (usually a launch arg).

clock.$comment: The app's own 'now' (the status bar's is the plan's clock) and how it's fixed. On-screen times usually need a screenshot mode; without one, pick screens that show none, or say so.

network.$comment: offline (fixtures), mock (a local fake server), staging (a staging server with invented data) or live (discouraged).

args.$comment: Launch arguments (iOS -Key value), intent extras (Android), query parameters (web).

clean.$comment: Reinstall or clear the app's data first.

into.$comment: The field to type into, found by its text (placeholder).

flow.$comment: A Maestro flow's path or a UI test's name (string), or the flow driver's own object.

appFile.$comment: Copy a file into the app's own data, the app stopped first (simctl's data container; Android's data folder through run-as, debug builds). Drivers with a host do it through the host.

ignore.$comment: Rectangles [x, y, width, height] in the picture's pixels left out of the comparison (an animation that never stops).
